newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise despite high German data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise despite high German data.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Thursday despite higher than expected German January Ifo business climate and M3 money supply data with prices seen holding in a solid market.
"The price rises seem a bit illogical when you consider the German data but it just goes to show how solidly rooted the market is here," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.07 point from the start at 112.18, yielding 6.20 percent in turnover of 3.6 billion crowns while its March future fell 0.38 point to 111.78 with 674 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.20 point to 89.80.
The crown traded at 3.8159 per mark at 1250 gmt, virtually the same as around 3.8160 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 66.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling an unspecified amount of five percent 2005 state bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
